facts.text: The repository is built on Evogym, a simulation environment for evolutionary robotics and soft robots
The package requires Python >=3.7 and <3.11
The package depends on gymnasium and numpy<2.0.0
Installation builds the CMake extension evogym.simulator_cpp from evogym/simulator
WalkingFlat is the concrete environment class of evogym.envs.walk
Walker-v0 is registered with entry point evogym.envs.walk:WalkingFlat and max_episode_steps=500
WalkingFlat loads the Walker-v0 world and adds the robot body at position (1, 1)
The number of action values is the number of actuator indices of the robot
num_robot_points is the size of the robot's position array
The action space is Box(low=0.6, high=1.6, shape=(num_actuators,))
The observation space is Box(low=-100.0, high=100.0, shape=(2 + num_robot_points,))
The environment's step forwards the robot action to the base step as a one-entry robot dictionary
EvoGymBase.step clips every actuator value to [0.6, 1.6] before setting it
The observation concatenates the robot's centre-of-mass velocity with its relative point positions
get_relative_pos_obs subtracts the point centre and flattens the coordinate array
The reward is the change of the robot's centre-of-mass x between the previous and the new step
An unstable simulation subtracts 3.0 from the reward
The goal is met when the centre-of-mass x exceeds 99 voxel sizes and adds 1.0 to the reward
WalkingFlat.step returns five values and always reports truncated=False
WalkingFlat.reset calls the base reset and returns the observation with an empty info dict
EvoGymBase.reset ignores its seed and options arguments and resets the simulator
BenchmarkBase.VOXEL_SIZE is 0.1
The simulator runs physics_updates_per_step=30 updates per environment step
Each physics update integrates 0.0001 s with the RK4 integrator
The project's own test constructs an environment with gym.make(env_name, body=body)
The Walker-v0 example supplies a body from sample_robot((5,5))
The voxel types define H_ACT as 3 and V_ACT as 4

determinism.notes: the fake's transitions are deterministic and the upstream reset ignores seed and options (base.py:65-69, walk.py:74-84), so a reset reproduces the same initial state with or without a seed; the bridge still advertises cap.world.seed.v1 because the reset signature accepts seed, but the value does not change the initial state or the fake trajectory

gaps: no soft-body simulation: the C++ point-mass physics, actuator deformation, contacts, collisions, constraint solving and self-collision instability flag are not modelled

the fake moves a single centre of mass at a placeholder gain from the mean clipped actuator value and holds four material points at fixed relative offsets; it is an F0 stand-in, not a re-implementation of the upstream dynamics

the observation has 2 + 2*4 = 10 values (four placeholder material points); the upstream size is 2 + num_robot_points (walk.py:34), where num_robot_points comes from the compiled simulator and the robot body, so the fake's array is a placeholder whose size is not the device's

the fake's body is a placeholder 5x5 robot with one horizontal actuator; the upstream body is the required body argument of WalkingFlat.__init__ (walk.py:17-27) and may have any valid shape and actuator count, so the action width is a placeholder configuration, not a device property; the derived action bounds have fake provenance and no action_space_ref
the fake applies the 500-step time limit that gymnasium.make adds to Walker-v0 (evogym/envs/__init__.py:19); WalkingFlat.step itself always returns truncated=False (walk.py:72)

no sim backend is declared and the upstream environment was never run here: it needs Python <3.11, gymnasium, numpy<2.0.0 and the compiled evogym.simulator_cpp, and gym.make('Walker-v0') requires a robot body argument; package code never imports the clone
the fake returns Python floats and lists; upstream returns NumPy arrays and declares its Box spaces with dtype=float (walk.py:36-37)
no rendering and no snapshot or restore: the fake exposes no renderer or get_state/set_state
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor is 0 and only ticks advance the 3 ms simulated timestep

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
